transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came in because I can’t stop thinking about the left side of my face. My nose and jaw look crooked to me, especially in ID photos or on the online class camera. People tell me they don’t see it, but I feel like everyone in the CNC lab notices it before they notice anything I do.
Because of how your face looks to you, do you find yourself checking mirrors or cameras over and over?

Yeah. Before school I can get stuck in the bathroom checking the mirror, then my phone camera, over and over. I’ll fix my hair or change shirts because I’m trying to hide the angle of my face. I ask my mom if it looks weird too. Sometimes it takes so long I miss lab, or I get there exhausted and can’t focus.
Do you avoid being around other people because you’re afraid they’ll judge the way your face looks?

Yeah. I’ve missed CNC labs and shop shifts because I just couldn’t make myself go out where people might look at me. My faculty mentor said my work placement could be in jeopardy now. I stopped playing soccer and volunteering too, because I don’t want people staring at my face.
If you didn’t have these worries about your face, would you still feel afraid of being around other people?
I’m not sure. I guess I’d probably be more comfortable going to lab and being around people if I wasn’t worrying about how my face looks all the time.
At your deepest level, do you believe there really is something wrong with the way your face looks?

Yeah, I do. I know people tell me they don’t see it, but the left side of my face looks wrong to me—like my nose and jaw are crooked, especially in ID photos or on the online class camera. It feels like people in the CNC lab notice that before they notice anything else about me.
Do you spend a lot of time each day thinking about the way your face looks?

Yeah. It’s on my mind most of the day. I keep thinking about how the left side looks off—my nose and jaw, especially if I see myself on the class camera or in an ID photo. Even when people say they don’t notice it, I feel like people in the CNC lab see it before they see anything else.
Do you try to hide the left side of your face from other people?

Yeah. Before school I’ll spend a long time in the bathroom mirror or using my phone camera, trying to get my hair right or changing shirts so the angle doesn’t show as much. I’ll ask my mom if it looks weird too. Sometimes I do it for so long I’m late for lab, or I get there too exhausted to focus.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
I’m not sure. I know I feel bad about how I look a lot, but I don’t really know if I’d call it depressed most days.
Outside of worries about your face, are you afraid that people will judge or embarrass you in social situations?
I’m not really sure. Mostly I worry about people seeing my face. I don’t know if I’m afraid of social situations otherwise.
Do you also get unwanted thoughts that keep coming back over and over about things other than your appearance?
Not that I’ve noticed. It’s mainly the appearance stuff—I don’t really have other thoughts that keep repeating like that.
Has a doctor or dentist ever told you that your nose or jaw is noticeably crooked?
No, nobody’s actually told me that. But I see it all the time—the left side looks off to me, like my nose and jaw are crooked, especially in ID photos or on the online class camera.
When other people look at your face in person, do they usually say they can see the crookedness too?

Most people say they don’t see it, or they say my face looks normal. But I don’t really believe them. I feel like people in the CNC lab notice the left side of my face before they even notice my work.
To other people, would you say the problem with the left side of your face is only slight or not really visible?

No, I don’t think it’s slight. Other people say they can’t see it, but in photos and on the class camera it looks really obvious to me. I feel like people in the CNC lab notice that side of my face before anything else.
Is it possible that your face actually looks normal and that this might be your mind focusing on it too much?

I mean, maybe that’s what people are telling me, but I can’t see it that way. Every time I see an ID photo or the online class camera, the left side looks crooked to me—my nose and jaw. I keep thinking people in the CNC lab notice that before they notice my work.
Are you absolutely certain that the left side of your face is crooked?

Yeah… I’m pretty certain. When I see myself in ID photos or on the class camera, the left side—my nose and jaw—looks crooked. People tell me they don’t notice it, but I feel like they must, especially at the CNC lab.
Because of this worry about your face, have you been feeling sad or empty most days?
I’m not sure. I know I feel bad about how my face looks, but I don’t really know if I’d call it sad or empty most days.
Do you believe with complete certainty that your face is actually deformed?
I don’t know about completely certain, but it really looks deformed to me. The left side of my nose and jaw just seems crooked in photos and on the class camera, and I can’t stop noticing it.
When people are not able to see your face, do you still feel afraid they’ll judge or embarrass you?
I’m not really sure. I mostly worry about it when people can actually see me or when I see my face on camera.
When you check mirrors or your phone camera, does it briefly relieve the distress you feel about your face?

Yeah, but only for a minute. I keep checking the mirror or my phone camera before school, trying to fix my hair or change shirts so the angle doesn’t look as bad. Then I just end up checking again, and sometimes I’m doing it so long I miss lab or get there too wiped out to focus.
If you were not worried about how your face looks, would you still be afraid of being judged by other people?
No, I don’t think so. It’s mainly because I feel like the left side of my face looks crooked. I keep thinking people in the CNC lab notice that before they notice anything else I’m doing.
